transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Ruiz (Paragon Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Paragon ML Eng), Carlos Mendez (Paragon Security), Lina Ortega (Paragon Product)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — I'm Maya, AE for the region, and Jordan is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Ethan Ruiz: Hi Maya, hi Jordan. Ethan here, head of platform at Paragon. We're really trying to figure out the playbook for LLM features across customer support and ops.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Priya, ML engineer, I'll be running the evals and the pilot.
[00:19] Carlos Mendez: Carlos, security. I'll be looking at KMS, audit logs, and data residency.
[00:23] Jordan Patel: Great. We'll walk through model choices first, then runtime/deploy options, and wrap with next steps. Sound good?

--- Quick context / qualification ---
[00:40] Jordan Patel: Can you tell us the main customer-facing use cases and any hard constraints on latency, throughput, and PII?
[00:46] Ethan Ruiz: Sure. Two use cases: automated support summarization + triage and an internal ops assistant to parse shipment manifests. Latency target for support snippets is sub 1s for short queries, but for multi-turn summarization we can live with a couple seconds. Throughput is modest — maybe 30 reqs/sec peak initially. Data: some PII in transcripts, so encryption and audit logging are musts. Also we have international customers — Spanish and Portuguese primarily, some French.
[01:15] Priya Nair: For context length, we expect a lot of long conversations; some threads run 6-12k tokens if you include metadata. We want to compare 8k vs 32k window models.

--- Model selection conversation ---
[01:40] Maya Chen: Ok perfect. For open models we're usually recommending a shortlist depending on your length and multilingual needs. Jordan, want to give a quick list?
[01:47] Jordan Patel: Yeah. For 8k contexts, the family that tends to be best in our infra is the Llama-derived 2.x variants and Mistral medium/large for instruction. For 32k, there are models with extended context like trimmed Llama-extended or specialized long-context models. We also see quality wins in certain multilingual checkpoints from community forks. Important note: quantization and kernels impact latency — some 32k variants need optimized kernels that only run well on Dedicated hardware.
[02:18] Ethan Ruiz: When you say 'only on Dedicated' — do you mean Redwood Hosted won't serve 32k reliably?
[02:23] Jordan Patel: Hosted can, but there are tradeoffs. Hosted has shared capacity and we route by performance profile. For consistent latency at 32k with large batch, Dedicated gives control of the GPU type and kernel stack; otherwise you might see jitter. Also caching behavior for long KV caches is more tunable on Dedicated/Private.
[02:45] Priya Nair: How do you recommend we evaluate multilingual quality? We need Spanish/French to be as accurate as English.
[02:51] Jordan Patel: We recommend building a small eval set of 200 real dialogues in each language and run both zero-shot and few-shot with and without retrieval. We'll also measure hallucination rates on named entities. We can share a template for that.
[03:05] Maya Chen: We'll include some sample prompts and a spreadsheet to track ROUGE/Exact-match plus a small human eval rubric.

--- Tool calling and security concerns ---
[03:22] Carlos Mendez: Important: any external tool calling — e.g., hitting our order API or internal systems — must be auditable and go through our service account. We cannot allow arbitrary outbound internet from any component processing PII.
[03:36] Jordan Patel: Understood. Redwood supports function/tool calling and you can lock down tool endpoints to a VPC or internal-only endpoints for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can also do tool calling but we'd require egress rules and we can provide a proxy pattern; we also support credential injection via KMS so the model runtime doesn't persist your keys.
[03:57] Carlos Mendez: KMS integration is critical. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:01] Maya Chen: Yes, we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted, we have a bring-your-own-key flow that integrates with major KMS providers — we'll include the docs.

--- Cost / latency tradeoffs and quantization ---
[04:15] Priya Nair: Cost is a big factor. If we choose a 32k model, token costs go up and GPU footprint too. How aggressive are your quantization recommendations?
[04:24] Jordan Patel: We have quantization profiles and will recommend per-model settings. For many production workloads, 4-bit quantized weights on certain kernels provide 2-3x cost reductions with limited quality loss, but some multilingual or instruction-following checkpoints regress. We always suggest a short eval to compare quality vs cost. Also automatic prefix/KV caching can cut token usage significantly for repeated contexts.
[04:50] Ethan Ruiz: What about throughput guarantees? If we go Dedicated, do we get predictable p99 latency?
[04:56] Jordan Patel: Yes — Dedicated comes with SLA-backed throughput and configurable autoscaling. You can define latency SLOs and fallback policies to cheaper model variants if the primary is overloaded.

--- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision factors ---
[05:15] Lina Ortega: From a product lens, we want fast experiments and then a stable production path. Hosted is fastest to test, Dedicated is predictable, Private is for strict compliance. Anything else to consider?
[05:25] Maya Chen: Exactly. Hosted is great for rapid iteration and we can give you isolated routing policies in the hosted tier. Dedicated is for predictable economics and performance. Private (VPC/on-prem) is mainly for customers with regulatory or network-isolation needs — you manage the control plane and keys. There's also a hybrid approach: start on Hosted for the pilot and move to Dedicated once you have steady load.

--- Technical deep-dive snippets (Jordan) ---
[05:50] Jordan Patel: Some things to watch during your evals: sequence length distribution, batch sizes, and how often you hit the KV cache. If your average sequence is short but you occasionally need 30k tokens, a routing policy that sends short calls to a cheaper 8k model and long calls to a long-context model can be optimal. Also tool-calling state must be checkpointed carefully — avoid leaking tokens to logs and use redact hooks.
[06:18] Priya Nair: About logs — we need full audit logs for calls and ability to purge.
[06:23] Jordan Patel: Redwood has per-request metadata and audit logs, retention policies, and you can configure log sinks to your SIEM. For Hosted, retention defaults are configurable; for Dedicated and Private you control retention and storage.

--- Mis-transcribed/misheard moment (typical) ---
[06:40] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[06:44] Maya Chen: Sorry, small crosstalk — Jordan mentioned K-V cash, I think he meant KV cache.

--- Example case study and pilot scope ---
[06:55] Maya Chen: Quick example: a customer we worked with had multilingual support and started on Hosted using an 8k model with retrieval for older context. They hit a quality plateau for transcripts that required 20k context, so they moved to Dedicated with a long-context variant and saw better 99th percentile latency and lower cost due to batching.
[07:15] Ethan Ruiz: That sounds similar to what we might do. For pilot scope, here's what we want: 1) run a 2-week hosted trial on a mirrored subset of support traffic, 2) evaluate English/Spanish quality, 3) measure latency and token cost, 4) run a failover exercise where we simulate heavy load.
[07:35] Jordan Patel: We can support that. For the hosted trial we'll provide a sandbox API key and a routing policy. We'll also instrument cost telemetry for token-level breakdowns.

--- Questions from Priya (eval specifics) ---
[07:50] Priya Nair: When you say routing policy, can it do model version pinning by conversation id?
[07:55] Jordan Patel: Yes, you can pin model versions per route or per conversation ID, and you can automate rollouts with canary and A/B via the console.
[08:05] Priya Nair: For tool calling, can we sandbox side-effecting calls during eval?
[08:09] Jordan Patel: Absolutely. You can configure tool stubs for the trial so side effects are simulated, then switch to real endpoints in Dedicated or Private.

--- Security deep-dive (Carlos) ---
[08:20] Carlos Mendez: A few specific asks: SOC 2 report, ISO scope, how long tokens are retained in cache, and if there is any ephemeral storage that might persist PII. Also we need SAML SSO + RBAC for team access.
[08:35] Maya Chen: We'll send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts. Token caching is controlled by policy — you can disable persistent cache for Hosted, or use private VPC where caches are customer-controlled. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported across tiers.
[08:51] Carlos Mendez: What about attestations for data residency? We have EU clients and need any EU data to stay in region.
[08:58] Jordan Patel: Redwood's hosted regions cover EMEA; you can pin region routing so requests stay in EU. For absolute guarantees we recommend Private or Dedicated with EU region placement.

--- Pilot logistics and timeline ---
[09:15] Ethan Ruiz: If we start the hosted pilot next week, how fast can you spin up the sandbox?
[09:20] Maya Chen: We can provide sandbox creds within 2 business days once we have a signed trial AUP. Jordan will help with the routing policy template.
[09:27] Jordan Patel: I'll also share a short checklist: sample size, languages, key eval metrics, and suggested model variants for 8k vs 32k.

--- Pricing signal briefly ---
[09:40] Maya Chen: High level, Dedicated pricing is committed monthly capacity, cheaper per-token for heavy steady traffic. Hosted is pay-as-you-go. We'll share ballpark numbers in the follow-up.

--- Closing recap and next steps ---
[09:56] Maya Chen: Quick recap: we'll send security/compliance docs, Jordan will provide benchmark checklist and sample routing policy, and Priya will share sample dialogues. You'll kick off a hosted trial for a 2-week mirror.
[10:10] Ethan Ruiz: Sounds good. Carlos, anything else from security?
[10:14] Carlos Mendez: Just that we need the SOC doc and network diagram before we spin up any test keys.
[10:20] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize that — you'll have them by Tuesday.
[10:23] Lina Ortega: Who's the point person for the trial?
[10:26] Ethan Ruiz: Priya will own the trial from our side.
[10:29] Maya Chen: Great. We'll schedule the pricing/deep cost review next week — propose Wednesday.
[10:33] Priya Nair: Wednesday works. I'll also share the sample dataset by end of day Friday.
[10:37] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and the onboarding link.
[10:42] Ethan Ruiz: Thanks all.
[10:44] (call ends)
